title: Siding Painting
heading: A New Colour for the Siding You Have.
intro: Siding painting can update your home’s exterior while retaining sound existing panels. We identify the siding material, inspect its condition and recommend preparation, colour and coating options suited to your property in Southern Ontario.
explain: Painting Siding Starts With the Material
paragraphs: Wood, aluminum, vinyl and other siding products do not need the same treatment. Existing coatings, moisture, panel damage and manufacturer requirements all affect the plan. Knowing the material is the first step toward deciding whether painting is a suitable option.

We discuss full exterior repaints and smaller siding updates, including how the colour will work with the roof, masonry and trim. Preparation and application are tailored to the substrate rather than treating every wall as the same surface.
prepare: Clean and dry the siding, remove unstable coating, and complete the agreed preparation and any necessary priming.
apply: Use a coating and application method suited to the identified siding material and its existing finish.
condition: Peeling, swelling, cracks and moisture damage need assessment. Painting will not repair failing siding panels.
material: Vinyl colour restrictions, aluminum chalking and wood movement require different preparation and product choices.
goals: Decide whether you want all elevations repainted or a smaller refresh with coordinated trim and accents.
tip: Share the siding material if known, along with photos of any damaged or peeling sections.

title: Aluminum Siding Painting
heading: Refresh Faded Siding Without Starting Over.
intro: Aluminum siding painting gives sound metal panels a fresh colour without replacing the exterior. We assess chalking, previous coatings and exposed metal, then plan cleaning and a compatible finish for your Southern Ontario property.
paragraphs: Yes, sound aluminum siding can often be repainted. A faded factory finish does not automatically mean the panels need replacement. The assessment checks coating adhesion, dents, corrosion and repairs before deciding what painting can reasonably improve.

Chalky residue needs particular attention because new paint must adhere to the surface beneath it. Cleaning, drying and any required priming are followed by a coating suitable for aluminum. Matching nearby trim helps make the finished exterior feel cohesive.
prepare: Remove chalk and surface contamination, deal with loose coating, and prime exposed metal or other areas as the product requires.
apply: Apply a compatible exterior coating evenly across the prepared panels, including edges and profiles within the agreed scope.
condition: Chalking, peeling and exposed metal affect adhesion. Damaged panels or corrosion may require repair beyond painting.
material: Confirm the siding is aluminum and review the existing finish before choosing cleaning, primer and coating products.
goals: Compare repainting with replacement based on the panels’ condition, the colour you want and any repairs needed.
tip: Photograph chalky areas, exposed metal and damaged panels before your quote discussion.
benefits: Choose colours that work with the roof, trim and fixed materials.

title: Vinyl Siding Painting
heading: A Fresh Colour With Vinyl in Mind.
intro: Vinyl siding painting can refresh faded panels when the material is sound and the colour is suitable. We check the existing siding and manufacturer guidance before discussing a coating system for your Southern Ontario home.
paragraphs: Sound vinyl siding can be painted with a compatible product and appropriate preparation. Split, loose or warped panels need separate attention. Painting changes the appearance of the surface; it does not correct installation problems or restore damaged siding.

Colour selection is especially important. Darker colours can increase heat absorption, so the coating palette and siding manufacturer’s instructions need to agree. We review colour suitability, cleaning, drying and application requirements before recommending a vinyl siding repaint.
prepare: Wash away contamination, allow the vinyl to dry, and prepare or prime according to the selected coating instructions.
apply: Apply a compatible coating in an approved colour under suitable surface and weather conditions.
condition: Cracked, warped or poorly secured panels need assessment before a colour change. Painting cannot make them structurally sound.
material: Check both siding and paint manufacturer guidance. A colour suitable for another substrate may be unsuitable for vinyl.
goals: Bring colour ideas, but leave room to choose a shade approved for the existing vinyl and coating system.
tip: Keep any siding brand, warranty or installation details available for the assessment.
benefits: Choose colours that work with the roof, trim and fixed materials.

title: Wood Siding Painting

paragraphs: Wood expands and contracts with changing conditions, so the existing coating and timber condition need close attention. Loose paint, exposed grain, soft boards and damp areas all affect the scope. Rotten or failing sections need repair before a new finish is applied.

We discuss the look you want and whether paint or another suitable finish fits the siding. Bare wood and staining may need specific priming, while old coatings need preparation for adhesion. Colour, access and drying conditions are reviewed with the project plan.

apply: Apply a suitable exterior wood coating with attention to grain, joints and the product’s drying requirements.

material: The wood species, previous finish and exposure influence primer and coating selection.
goals: Discuss colour, visible grain and maintenance expectations before deciding on the finish.

title: Brick Painting & Staining
heading: A Considered Colour Change for Masonry.
intro: Brick painting and staining offer different ways to update suitable masonry. We review the brick, mortar, moisture and existing finishes before discussing which approach suits your Southern Ontario property.
paragraphs: Painting can create an opaque, coordinated finish, while a compatible masonry stain may retain more of the brick’s variation. The options depend on the masonry, previous treatments and whether a test area accepts the proposed product.

Moisture, damaged faces, salt deposits and failing mortar need attention before either treatment. We discuss the scope, product requirements and a suitable sample area rather than treating colour as a repair for masonry problems.
prepare: Review moisture and repair needs, clean suitable masonry and let it dry. Agree on product-specific preparation and any test area before painting or staining.
apply: Apply the selected masonry paint or stain in suitable conditions, following its preparation, coverage and drying instructions.
condition: Moisture, salt deposits, damaged faces and failing mortar need assessment before coating the brick.
material: Brick and mortar are porous. Paint forms a surface coating; a suitable masonry stain changes colour differently and depends on absorption, existing coatings and the exact product system.
goals: Compare the appearance, surface condition and future maintenance of paint and stain before choosing an approach.
tip: Point out damp patches, salt deposits and previous masonry repairs during the assessment.
benefits: Choose colours that work with the roof, trim and fixed materials.
